svg.title: Losing an acknowledgement does not create another logical message
svg.desc: Asha sends client identity phone-uuid-7. The conversation transaction checks current membership and commits sequence1, its retry fingerprint and outbox. The acceptance response is lost. Retrying the same sender identity and bytes returns C42/1; the log still has one message. Device delivery and read receipts are separate later facts.
svg.text: A stable client identity resolves an uncertain send
Conversation C42 · sender A · clientMessageId phone-uuid-7 · same text on retry.
1. Validate current membership and resolve prior request identity
The same ID with different bytes is a conflict. A different ID is a different logical message.
Sequence 1 + C42/1 + retry fingerprint/result + delivery outbox
A real database adapter must commit before returning ACCEPTED; the local monitor models this boundary.
3. Response disappears; Asha retries the same operation
No response is not evidence that the transaction failed.
4. Return ACCEPTED C42/1 again; do not append sequence 2 for this retry
The durable log remains the recovery path even if gateway delivery fails.
Source accepted ≠ phone received ≠ laptop received ≠ user reported read.
